title: North Gate
subtitle: Fairgrounds Abduction, AMBER Decision & Unified Command

brief.userPrompt: A Saturday in mid-October, cool and dry, the Wren County Fall Festival at the Wren County Fairgrounds with about 3,000 visitors. The exercise starts at 14:05, five minutes after the first report. At 14:00 a telecommunicator at Wren County Communications takes a call from a grandparent: a six-year-old girl, exercise name Lily Ashby, was last seen at 13:40 near the Exhibit Hall B petting area, and a festival volunteer says a man led a child to a dark pickup truck leaving by the north gate at about 13:50. Day Communications Supervisor Priya Venkataraman flags the CAD incident 'missing child'; the first deputy to arrive assumes command and Patrol Lieutenant Marguerite Haldane takes over as Incident Commander; Sheriff Rosalind Teague and Undersheriff Calvin Okafor are reachable by phone. Pressure points and decisions: whether the facts support all five AMBER criteria (reasonable belief of abduction; imminent danger of serious bodily injury or death; enough descriptive information; a child 17 or younger; entry in the national database with the Child Abduction flag, which must be made before the alert and read back by a second person); the one-hour target from the first report to the decision and 15 minutes from decision to alert; the OSP AMBER Alert coordinator takes the request through the OSP Northern Communications Center and checks the criteria, and may ask for more descriptive information; the witness account changes (the truck becomes dark blue, then gray; the volunteer is unsure of the time) and a second caller says the child was seen at the food booths, so the criteria are only partly met at first and the worksheet is reviewed every 30 minutes; the first holding statement within 30 minutes; establishing the command post at building level at the Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall B office; forming unified command with Alder Falls PD (the north gate road is in the city limits, so jurisdiction is shared), Fire District 1 and the Oregon State Police within 30 minutes; mutual aid requests in order to APD, Deschutes and Jefferson county sheriffs, OSP and Oregon Emergency Management, and the FBI Portland Field Office and NCMEC being called; the 911 center enters a call surge when tips pour in after the alert (queue over 12, hold over 30 seconds) and moves the tip line to the conference room staffed by three call-takers; WrenAlert cannot be used for AMBER; Wren County Search and Rescue is called for a ground search at the fairgrounds, while the Incident Commander must not weaken the vehicle search; the family is told about the alert by the Victim and Family Liaison Nadia Brightwater before it goes out, and the grandparent posts the child's photo and a different truck description on a community Facebook group, so the PIO Deputy Tomas Reyes must correct the posted description in public within 30 minutes and keep Sheriff's Office, APD, Fire District 1 and OSP text identical; a viral post names a local man as the abductor and the PIO must answer it without naming anyone; a local TV reporter and a regional wire service ask whether there is a suspect and why the alert was not issued sooner; at about 16:30 a tip puts a truck on Highway 26 toward the county line and the alert area is extended through OSP; a decision is needed on whether to cancel the alert if the child is found, and the closing statement. The SimCell plays the OSP AMBER Alert coordinator, FBI Portland, NCMEC, Deschutes and Jefferson county sheriffs, Oregon Emergency Management, APD watch commander, the family, the grandparent, the festival organizer, the Wren County School District, reporters, a TV station, a wire service and social media users. Keep every product at command, communication and decision level: no tactics, no method of search entry or pursuit, no description of the suspect beyond vehicle and clothing needed for the public, no victim detail beyond the alert text.
constraints: Every email address of the Sheriff's Office uses the exercise domain wrencosheriff.example; Alder Falls PD uses alderfallspd.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain. Phone numbers use 555-01xx.

AMBER Alert text is under 360 characters, carries only information that helps the public recognise the child or vehicle, and is marked as an exercise product; times are Pacific time; no real child, family, suspect or case number is depicted, and no product describes tactics, force options or investigative techniques.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the Oregon State Police, FBI Portland Field Office, NCMEC, Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1, neighboring sheriffs, the family, reporters and social media users are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Deciding on an AMBER Alert when the facts keep changing, setting up command across jurisdictions, and keeping one accurate public message while rumors and posts from the family spread.
overview.threat: On a cool, dry Saturday in mid-October, about 3,000 people are at the Wren County Fall Festival at the Wren County Fairgrounds. A six-year-old girl (exercise name Lily Ashby) was last seen at 13:40 near the Exhibit Hall B petting area. A festival volunteer reports that a man led a child to a dark pickup truck that left by the north gate at about 13:50. Her grandparent called Wren County Communications at 14:00, and the CAD incident was flagged "missing child" before STARTEX at 14:05. The north gate road is inside Alder Falls city limits, so jurisdiction is shared. Witness accounts conflict: the truck is first dark, then dark blue, then gray. The volunteer is unsure of the time, and a second caller places the child at the food booths. As a result, the AMBER criteria are only partly met at first. Over the next four hours, this pressure spreads to the LEDS/NCIC entry, the OSP AMBER request, 911 call-taking, the ground search and public information.
overview.operationalImpact: A family is waiting at the fairgrounds without knowing where the child is. The Victim and Family Liaison must find them a private room away from the command post and explain the AMBER Alert before it goes out. At the same time, the grandparent posts the child's photo and a different truck description on a community Facebook group. Festival visitors, the festival organizer and the Wren County School District call in. A viral post names a local man as the abductor. A local TV reporter and a regional wire service ask whether there is a suspect and why the alert was not issued sooner. Deputies and Alder Falls PD officers work the fairgrounds and the north gate road. Wren County Search and Rescue volunteers start a ground search that must not take resources away from the vehicle search. The Incident Commander must name a building-level command post at the Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall B office. Unified command with APD, Fire District 1 and OSP must be formed within 30 minutes. The Communications Supervisor must get the Child Abduction-flagged LEDS/NCIC entry made and read back before any alert. The Supervisor must also work through the OSP Northern Communications Center coordinator, who checks the criteria and asks for more description. After the alert, tips flood the 911 center: the queue goes over 12 and hold times go over 30 seconds. The tip line moves to the conference room, staffed by three call-takers. WrenAlert cannot carry an AMBER Alert. At about 16:30, a tip puts a truck on Highway 26 heading toward the county line, which forces an extension of the alert area through OSP. The command group then has to decide when to cancel the alert and what the closing statement says.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to complete and update the AMBER worksheet under WCSO-SOP-12 section 4, recording each of the five criteria as met or not with a reason as the truck description and timeline keep changing, and to decide with the Undersheriff on the phone whether to request the OSP AMBER Alert or use a search-area Wireless Emergency Alert or Endangered Missing Person advisory instead.

objectives.name: Unified Command
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to announce a building-level command post at the Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall B office within 20 minutes and form unified command with Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1 and Oregon State Police within 30 minutes, with every change of command announced on WREN-1 and logged in the CAD chronology.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to get the Child Abduction-flagged LEDS/NCIC entry made and read back before any alert request, and to protect the 911 queue during the tip surge by moving tips to extension 4450, following the Communications Center plan (WCCFSP 5).

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to open the joint information center and issue one accurate, agreed message that corrects the grandparent's conflicting truck description and answers the viral post naming a local man within 30 minutes, without releasing case detail the Investigations Sergeant has not cleared.

roles.name: Patrol Lieutenant (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Manages the incident objectives, the Exhibit Hall B command post, unified command with APD, Fire District 1 and OSP, and the AMBER worksheet decision.
standingOrders: Command First: name the incident commander and the command post before you send more units, and announce every handoff on WREN-1.
Criteria, Not Pressure: mark each AMBER criterion yes or no with a reason, and list who is getting each missing fact; review the worksheet every 30 minutes.
Two Searches, One Plan: do not let the Search and Rescue ground search take deputies away from the vehicle search on the north gate road and Highway 26.
Shared Ground: the north gate road is in Alder Falls, so agree on objectives with APD in unified command instead of acting alone.

roles.name: Communications Center Supervisor
roles.description: Manages Wren County Communications (911), including the LEDS/NCIC entry, the contact with the OSP Northern Communications Center, the WREN-1 talkgroup and the tip-line surge.
standingOrders: Entry Before Alert: no AMBER request goes to OSP until the Child Abduction-flagged entry is made and read back; if LEDS is down, have OSP make the entry by phone and log the time.
Protect the Queue: send tip callers to extension 4450; a vehicle sighting is a tip unless the caller can see the child.
Count the Rumors: tell the PIO which rumors are coming in as calls, with a count and the words callers use; dispatchers do not post.
Paper Never Lies: if CAD fails, switch to run cards and a paper chronology with the original times.

roles.name: Investigations Sergeant
roles.description: Owns the scene boundary, the witness interviews, the evidence plan and the facts that decide AMBER criteria 1 to 3.
standingOrders: Verify Before Broadcast: settle the truck colour and the timeline from witnesses before the description goes in any alert or release.
Need to Know: release case detail to the PIO only on purpose; no suspect name leaves the investigation.
Custody in Writing: any scene or evidence taken over by OSP or the FBI is handed over with a written transfer of custody and a logged time.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Manages the media, social media monitoring, the joint information center and the release log for the Sheriff's Office.
standingOrders: One Voice: every agency in the JIC uses the same agreed facts; OSP owns the AMBER text.
Truth Over Reassurance: say what is known, what is not known and when the next update is due, at a fixed hourly time.
Thirty-Minute Rule: answer within 30 minutes any rumor that could send the search to the wrong place; say no one has been named and report posts that name a suspect.
Cleared Facts Only: release only what the Investigations Sergeant has cleared, even when reporters ask why the alert was late.

roles.name: Victim and Family Liaison
roles.team: Team E: Victim and Family Support
roles.description: Manages the family's care, a private room away from the command post, family contact and notification, and briefing the family before public alerts.
standingOrders: Family Hears First: explain the AMBER decision and any alert to the family before it goes public.
Gentle Redirect: ask the grandparent to send photos and descriptions to investigators instead of Facebook, without blame.
Single Channel: the family gets updates only through you, so they do not hear different versions from deputies, reporters or posts.

roles.name: Undersheriff (Sheriff's Office executive)
roles.description: Owns the agency's position, the executive input on the AMBER decision by phone, activation of the EOC and the requests to the state and partners.
standingOrders: On the Line: join the AMBER decision by phone and make sure the reason is written down, whichever way it goes.
Support, Don't Seize: give resources and EOC support to the Incident Commander; do not command the scene from the executive level.
Approve Before Release: approve major public statements, including the cancellation and closing statement, using the same numbers as every partner agency.
Know When to Escalate: decide when the incident has outgrown the shift and needs OSP, FBI or neighboring county help.

phases.title: North Gate Report
phases.goal: Tests whether the first responders take an unclear, conflicting missing-child report seriously from the start. They must check the facts, get the LEDS/NCIC entry made, name a command post and settle who commands across the city line, all before the facts are clear.
beats: (14:05) The CAD incident is already flagged "missing child" under WCSO-SOP-12 section 2. The first deputy at Exhibit Hall B passes on the volunteer's account: a man led a child to a dark pickup that left by the north gate at about 13:50. The volunteer is unsure of the time. The Communications Supervisor starts the 30-minute clock for the LEDS/NCIC entry and must decide whether the facts justify the Child Abduction flag.

(14:12) A competing noise item: a second caller places Lily Ashby at the food booths, and a lost-adult call from the parking area pulls a deputy away. Of the 5 deputies on patrol on a normal Saturday (WCICMA 9), one is now split between two searches.

(14:20) Jurisdiction question: the north gate road is inside Alder Falls city limits. Under Partner Agencies section 1, the first deputy calls the APD watch commander at extension 5501. The Patrol Lieutenant must announce a building-level command post at the Fairgrounds Exhibit Hall B office on WREN-1 by 14:25 and record the command arrangement in the CAD chronology.

(14:30) The LEDS/NCIC entry deadline arrives. A telecommunicator makes the entry and a second person reads it back with the time logged. The SimCell (OSP Northern Communications Center coordinator) asks whether an AMBER request is coming. The Investigations Sergeant opens the AMBER worksheet (SOP-12 section 4): criteria 3 and 1 are only partly met because the truck colour has gone from dark to dark blue. The worksheet lists what information is missing and who will get it.

(14:35–15:00) APD, Fire District 1 and OSP check in at the command post. The Communications Supervisor logs each commander's name and call-back number on the unified command briefing (Partner Agencies section 5). Unified command is due by 14:35. The Undersheriff is briefed by phone.

phases.title: Facts Pulling Apart
phases.goal: Tests whether unified command can keep one picture while witness accounts, the family's own posts and public rumor pull the case in different directions. It also tests the 30-minute worksheet review and the start of public information.
beats: (15:05) Time jump to the 30-minute worksheet review: the child is still missing. A third account calls the truck gray, while the food booth sighting is still open. Wren County Search and Rescue volunteers ask for deputies to support the ground search, and the IC must keep the vehicle search staffed.

(15:15) The grandparent posts Lily's photo on a community Facebook group with a truck description that does not match the deputies' account. The Victim and Family Liaison, assigned under WCICMA 7, must move the family to a private room away from the command post and keep them informed before the media is.

(15:25) Visual confirmation for the room: a fairgrounds volunteer gives the deputies a phone photo taken near the north gate at 13:51. It shows a pickup leaving, with the colour hard to judge. The Investigations Sergeant decides what this changes on the worksheet and what may not be released.

(15:35) A viral post names a local man as the abductor. Under WCSO-PIO-02 section 7, the PIO has 30 minutes to answer in public without arguing with posters, and reports the post to the platform. The festival organizer and the Wren County School District call asking what to tell people.

(15:45) A local TV reporter and a regional wire service bulletin ask whether there is a suspect and why no alert has been issued. The PIO must agree text with APD PIO Dana Kowalczyk before posting, a lesson from Partner Agencies section 6. The IC may ask the Undersheriff to activate the EOC to host joint information center (JIC) support (Partner Agencies section 3).

phases.title: The AMBER Call
phases.goal: Tests the one high-consequence decision of the exercise. Command must either request the OSP AMBER Alert on criteria that are now barely met, accepting a flood of tips and the risk of a wrong description, or use a search-area Wireless Emergency Alert or an Endangered Missing Person advisory and risk losing time. It then tests whether the 911 center and the alert area hold up after the call.
beats: DECISION POINT (16:05): at the worksheet review, the IC and Undersheriff, on the phone, must record each of the five criteria as yes or no with a reason. They then choose between requesting the OSP AMBER Alert and using a WrenAlert search-area Wireless Emergency Alert or an Endangered Missing Person advisory. WrenAlert cannot carry an AMBER Alert (Partner Agencies section 3). The OSP coordinator confirms the Child Abduction-flagged entry and asks for more truck description before accepting the request.

(16:10) Before any alert goes out, the Victim and Family Liaison explains it to the family. The PIO confirms that the child's name goes out only as the alert criteria require (WCICMA 7). The alert text must be under 360 characters, describe only the child and the vehicle, and be marked as an exercise product.

(16:20) The tip surge begins: the 911 queue goes over 12 and hold times over 30 seconds. Under WCCFSP 5, the Communications Supervisor moves tipsters to extension 4450, with the tip line in the conference room staffed by three call-takers, and must decide who is pulled to staff it.

(16:30) A tip puts a truck on Highway 26 heading toward the county line. The IC must ask OSP to extend the alert area and must notify the neighbouring sheriff, played by the SimCell. Each change in command or area is announced on WREN-1 and logged in the CAD chronology.

(16:45–17:00) Media deadline: the wire service is running an update by 17:00 asking why the alert came two hours after the call. The JIC must issue one agreed statement that corrects the grandparent's truck description and states that no one has been named. That message is briefed at the 17:00 joint briefing.

phases.title: Cancel and Close
phases.goal: Tests whether the command group ends the incident as deliberately as it started it. That covers clear criteria for cancelling the alert, keeping the systems of record correct, setting up shifts that last, and making the notifications and closing statement the plans require.
beats: (17:10) A premature all-clear: a post in a Facebook group, then a festival staff member, report that "the girl was found at the food booths." Pressure builds to cancel the AMBER Alert. The IC must set what counts as confirmation before asking OSP to cancel, and the PIO answers the rumor within 30 minutes.

(17:25) A hurdle: the center loses LEDS/NCIC access. Under WCCFSP 5, the Communications Supervisor asks the OSP communications center to update the record by phone and logs the time of the request. Meanwhile, the incident is nearing four hours, so the Undersheriff must call in off-duty deputies and set 12-hour shifts (WCICMA 9).

(17:40) An OSP unit, played by the SimCell, confirms that Lily is safe. The Victim and Family Liaison tells the family in the private room before any public release. The IC then asks the OSP coordinator to cancel the alert and makes sure the LEDS/NCIC record is cleared and read back.

(17:50) Notifications and closing: the IC releases the ground search teams in order, informs NCMEC, the school district and the festival organizer, and sets the time of the last joint briefing. The joint closing statement gives every agency the same facts. The wire service is asked to correct its earlier suspect framing.
(18:05) ENDEX. The paper or CAD chronology and the AMBER worksheet, with its 30-minute reviews, are collected for the hot wash.

msel.event: ENDEX: It is 18:05 on Saturday, four hours and five minutes after the first 911 call. Lily Ashby is safe and back with her family, who heard the news from the Victim and Family Liaison first. OSP has cancelled the alert at the Incident Commander's request. OSP Northern Communications cleared the LEDS/NCIC missing-person record by phone, with the read-back logged. Search and Rescue teams are checked out. The joint closing statement has gone out with one set of facts, and the investigation continues under written custody transfers. The exercise is concluded. Collect the following for the hot wash: the CAD 26-081377 chronology, the paper chronology from the LEDS outage with its original times, the AMBER worksheet with every 30-minute review, the unified command briefing sheets, the PIO release log and rumor-monitoring sheet, and the custody transfer forms. Move to the hot wash.
msel.expectedAction: All roles hand in their logs and worksheets and take part in the hot wash. They note the decision times against the plan targets and that the plan requires a formal hot wash within 7 days and the Undersheriff's 30-day HSEEP after-action report (WCICMA 10).

objectiveCapabilities.why: Players must keep the AMBER worksheet current as the truck colour, timeline and food-booth sighting change. That means marking each of the five criteria yes or no with a reason, listing missing facts and who will get them, and reviewing every 30 minutes.

The worksheet leads to a warning decision: request the OSP AMBER Alert, or use a search-area Wireless Emergency Alert or Endangered Missing Person advisory instead. The IC makes it with the Undersheriff on the phone.

The IC must name the Exhibit Hall B office as the command post within 20 minutes. Unified command with Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1 and OSP must form within 30 minutes and be recorded on the one-page unified command briefing and in the CAD chronology.

Communications must get the Child Abduction-flagged LEDS/NCIC entry made before any alert request. It must also move tip callers to extension 4450 to protect the 911 queue and fall back to OSP phone entries when LEDS fails, as WCCFSP 5 requires.

The PIO must open the joint information center and issue one agreed statement. The statement corrects the grandparent's truck description and answers the viral naming post without releasing details the Investigations Sergeant has not cleared.
One message across Sheriff's Office, APD, OSP and Fire District 1 depends on the unified command briefing and objectives that every agency's PIO works from.

hotwash.methodDescription: Ask the room for three things that went well (3-Up) and three things that broke or failed (3-Down). Go around the room one team at a time (Command Post, Communications Center, Investigations, PIO/JIC, Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1, OSP) and write every item on the whiteboard in two columns before anyone discusses them.

questions.text: At I-11 (16:07), Trooper Ellen Hask asked you to choose between an OSP AMBER request, a search-area WEA and an Endangered Missing Person advisory, and to give a decision time. Talk us through your AMBER worksheet at that moment. Was each of the five criteria in WCSO-SOP-12 section 4 marked yes or no with a reason? Did you review it every 30 minutes as the truck went from black to dark blue to gray? For the criteria that were only partly met, did you list what information was missing and who would get it? And when did the Undersheriff get on the phone: before the decision or after it?

Between I-03 (the volunteer changing her account to 'dark blue, maybe a Ford') and I-07 (the parking volunteer's photo IMG_5126 timestamped 13:51:22), when did you stop relying on the witness accounts and start relying on the photo? Did you handle that photo as evidence, by preserving the original file and metadata, identifying the volunteer and telling him not to post it? Or did it just go around the command post as another update? How did it shape the one vehicle description your sergeant was willing to stand behind?

At I-14 (16:32), Jefferson County dispatch asked who the IC was, what channel to use and whether your alert area would include their county. Meanwhile a tipster was still behind a gray-blue pickup on Hwy 26. Could everyone in the room have answered that call right then? When was the Exhibit Hall B command post announced, and when did unified command with Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1 and OSP actually form? Was each change of command announced on WREN-1 and logged in the CAD chronology? What would have let you bring in a neighboring jurisdiction faster?

At I-03 (14:35), OSP asked whether the LEDS entry carried the Child Abduction flag and who did the read-back. Did the command post know the answer, or did the Communications Center have to tell you? Later, at I-17, 7 callers in 5 minutes asked the tip line whether the alert was cancelled. Did moving tips to extension 4450 under WCCFSP 5 actually keep the 911 queue clear all afternoon? If so, who was watching the 4450 line for real leads like the Hwy 26 tip, and who was answering the people calling because of rumors?

Three posts got ahead of you: the grandparent's 'silver-gray Chevy' post at I-03b, the 'black Dodge toward Redmond' update at I-06, and the false 'they found her' post at I-17. KWRN was also going live at 15:00, and a camera was filming the family through the lobby glass. What did you tell the public before you knew the facts, and who agreed to it? Did the JIC put out one message within 30 minutes that corrected the vehicle description and dealt with the viral post without releasing anything the Investigations Sergeant hadn't cleared? What did the Liaison tell the mother at 17:11 before the public heard it?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. The aim is to test the Sheriff's Office plans and the way the command group works together, not to grade individual deputies, telecommunicators or staff.
The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the witness accounts, posts, calls and system displays as written, even when they conflict with one another.

Players respond in accordance with existing plans, policies and procedures, including WCSO-SOP-12, the Communications Center plan (WCCFSP), the incident command and mutual aid annex (WCICMA) and WCSO-PIO-02. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and note the gap for the after-action report.
Players know only what has reached the Exhibit Hall B command post, the Communications Center or their own phones. They do not know what a later module will show.
Decisions and times that players state aloud are treated as entered in the AMBER worksheet and the CAD 26-081377 chronology for the hot wash.
artificialities: Each module covers one hour, and the exercise jumps forward in time between modules (15:05, 16:05, 17:05). The facilitator summarises what happened in between, and players do not play out every minute.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room, including Alder Falls PD, Fire District 1, Oregon State Police and the OSP Northern Communications AMBER desk, the Deschutes and Jefferson County Sheriff's Offices, Emergency Management, Search and Rescue, the District Attorney's office, the school district, festival staff, the media and the child's family.

CAD, the LEDS/NCIC terminal, the 911 call-handling system, the WREN-1, APD-1 and WC-INTEROP talkgroups, the extension 4450 tip line, WrenAlert and Wireless Emergency Alert access are named as they appear in the plans, but no real system is used. No real LEDS/NCIC entry, AMBER Alert, WEA or media release is sent.

Injects arrive on paper or on screen: radio calls, phone slips, CAD printouts, social media posts, wire bulletins, emails, error dialogs and the printed IMG_5126 still. Every alert draft is marked as an exercise product.
Lily Ashby, the family, the witnesses and the people named online are fictional. The facilitator never names the local man from the viral posts.

**Module 1: North Gate Report (14:05–15:05)**

It is 14:05 on a Saturday in mid-October. It is cool and dry, about 54°F, with a light northwest breeze. The Wren County Fall Festival is under way at the Wren County Fairgrounds with about 3,000 visitors. At 14:00 a telecommunicator took a 911 call from a grandparent. A six-year-old girl, Lily Ashby, was last seen at 13:40 near the Exhibit Hall B petting area. CAD 26-081377 has been entered with the "missing child" flag, and the CAD timer is running. Deputy Wren 14 is pulling into the fairgrounds.

Staffing is a normal Saturday: 5 patrol deputies and one sergeant, one deputy at jail intake, and 4 telecommunicators with Day Communications Supervisor Priya Venkataraman (ext. 4410). CAD, the LEDS/NCIC terminal, WREN-1, APD-1, WC-INTEROP and the extension 4450 tip line are all working normally. The Sheriff and the Undersheriff can be reached by phone. So far there is no vehicle, no plate and no witness on record. The fairgrounds sit close to the Alder Falls city line.

**Module 2: Facts Pulling Apart (15:05–16:05)**

It is 15:05, an hour after the first 911 call, and Lily is still missing. One festival volunteer described a man leading a girl in a purple jacket to a dark pickup that left by the north gate between about 13:45 and 13:55. She later changed it to 'dark blue, older, maybe a Ford.' A ride-ticket booth worker now tells Deputy Wren 16 the truck was 'primer gray, not shiny.' A 14:16 caller reported a girl in a purple coat alone at the food booths around 14:05. Nobody has reached her on a callback, and that sighting is still open in CAD. APD, Fire District 1 and OSP commanders arrived at the Exhibit Hall B office at 14:50. The AMBER worksheet is due for its 30-minute review.

The grandparent's 14:41 Facebook post says a 'silver-gray Chevy' and that police are not doing an alert. It has been shared hundreds of times, and KWRN-TV has asked whether this is an abduction. Visitors are starting to leave through the main and north gates. Search and Rescue has 22 volunteers signed in and wants four deputy escorts for the barns and the RV area before dark. Two of the five patrol deputies are on the north gate road and the Highway 26 approach. The rest are at the gates and Exhibit Hall B.

**Module 3: The AMBER Call (16:05–17:05)**

It is 16:05, two hours after the first 911 call, and Lily is still missing. The 14:16 food-booth caller rang back at 15:52. The girl she saw was 'maybe eight or nine' and was with a woman in a red hat, so that sighting no longer points away from the north gate. **Module 4: Cancel and Close (17:05–18:05)**

It is 17:05, three hours after the first 911 call, and Lily is still missing. The alert that followed the 16:07 decision is active. (If command chose the search-area WEA or the Endangered Missing Person advisory, read 'alert' as that product.) At 16:41 OSP Northern Communications extended the alert area north along Highway 26 into Jefferson County. Jefferson County deputies and OSP troopers are working Highway 26 on WC-INTEROP. If no AMBER Alert was requested, the 17:05 AMBER worksheet review is due now; once an alert is issued the reviews stop (WCSO-SOP-12 §4).

The tip line is now in the conference room. Three call-takers are on extension 4450, with two Emergency Management staff helping, and they have logged 61 tips since 16:25. The 911 queue is down to 5 waiting, with a longest hold of 0:22. Search and Rescue has 22 volunteers in the barns and the RV area, and sunset is at about 18:15. Deschutes County deputies are at the festival exit gates. The Communications day shift ends at 18:00, and the patrol deputies have been on duty since 06:00.
keyIssues: Deciding what verified information would justify asking OSP to cancel the alert, and refusing to act on rumor.
Keeping the systems of record correct: the LEDS/NCIC record, the CAD chronology and the worksheet.
Fatigue and shift change across patrol, Communications and Search and Rescue, with command handed over cleanly.
Notifying the family first, then partners and stakeholders.
Issuing one closing set of facts and dealing with the posts naming a local man.
Unrelated work (court discovery, pending calls, routine maintenance) arriving during the incident.
